no_row_in_this_drop_carries_a_price.handling: price_jod_raw and price_jod_test_margin are null and needs_price_review is true, which renders "Price on request" on the card, the details page and the share card, and keeps the record off the landing-page collection (js/home-collection.js). Setting a price later is a one-field edit per record.
no_row_in_this_drop_carries_a_price.note: The Price column is populated for every older ref and empty for every new one.

held_back.reason: the same apartment as 155 — identical sheet row (Abdoun, 1st, 162 m², 3 bed, 3 bath) and the photographs show the same rooms: same zebra armchair, same horse print, same dining set and clock, same green kitchen. Two shoots of one unit. The 2026-08-04 import flagged 157 as a duplicate of 155 independently.

the 23 photographs cover more than one apartment — four to five distinct living rooms and two different white kitchens. Nothing in the folder says which set is 167, and a gallery mixing two units is worse than no gallery. Needs the sender to split the folder.

photo_rules.scope: root level of each 2026-<ref> folder only; the "New folder" subdirectories are the raw unsorted dump, exactly as in the previous import
photo_rules.exif: stripped — every file is re-encoded, so no camera or GPS data ships

photo_decisions.151: took the numbered set 00–09 (10); the 15 WhatsApp-named files alongside them re-shoot the same rooms
photo_decisions.163: took the numbered set 1–12 (12); the 7 WhatsApp-named files are a DIFFERENT apartment — dark modern kitchen and marble bathroom against this listing's chandeliers and blue velvet. Globbing the folder would have published two properties as one.
photo_decisions.166: 4.jpeg carries a "free version of Watermarkly" promo bar across the bottom; 5.jpeg is the same shot without it, so 4.jpeg was dropped
